title: I Let the Group-Study-Room Camera Catch the Nap They Booked as a Seminar

parts.text: I booked room D at 1:11 p.m. and group Pax had pillows on the table under a seminar hold. The screen said: BOOK FOR STUDY. NO SLEEPING. CAMERA ON. I was twenty-two, student, holding a room code. Pax shrugged. "Seminars are rest." I photographed the screen, the code, and the pillows in the cone. Then I asked for the room log. At 1:17 access services pinged why Pax's name was on a nap booking. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Access services can see pillows on the table in room D during my seminar-looking hold.

social.video_title: They booked a group-study room as a seminar and napped — Part 1/2
social.description: Study room, a camera cone, pillows on the table. I logged the nap. Would you have asked access services?

parts.text: Pax called it recovery until access asked for the still. I printed the log, the screen, and the photo. The pillows left. Pax booked study and told the next group recovery was always about optics. Optics is a word nappers use when cameras exist. Room policy now has a second line: SEMINARS ARE NOT BEDS. I keep room D. Pax brown-bags the jokes. The table finally looks like a code, not a dorm. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Room log, pillows gone, and a second line. Was recovery ever my code?
